clue.text: Pad set up; new beginning

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word for pad is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a wad is a pad of soft material, as of cotton wool

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a pad, perhaps a new flat, ready for a fresh start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns WAD into DAW in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is the start of the day, and figuratively any beginning, as in the dawn of an era.

clue.text: Mixture of scrap for all to see in books

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other, here the film rating inside the books

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the books of the Bible's first part
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A scrap of something mixed in among books, on show to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning anyone may watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a stew, a dish of mixed meat and vegetables, so it is a culinary mixture.

clue.text: Bargain goes fast after sale's first promoted

indicators.note: in a down clue, promoted says a letter rises to the top of the word

parts.note: to nip is to go quickly, as in nips to the shop

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word sale's

explanation.surface: A bargain sells quickly once the sale's first item is pushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promoted' lifts the last S of NIPS to the top of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is informal British for a bargain, something bought cheaply.

clue.text: Associate cut short offensive husband

indicators.note: cut short says the word for offensive loses its final letter

parts.note: an offensive is a military attack

explanation.surface: A colleague cuts off a rude husband mid-sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' removes K from ATTACK, leaving ATTAC.
explanation.definitionFit: To associate one thing with another is to attach it, linking or connecting the two.

clue.text: Overconfident birds on river

parts.note: cocks are male birds, especially roosters
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Cocky birds strutting along a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocksure means arrogantly certain of oneself, a synonym for overconfident.

clue.text: Pressure with rent as part of salary that's deficient

indicators.note: as part of says the two pieces sit inside the word for salary

parts.note: salary is a person's income
P is the physics symbol for pressure
to let is to rent out a property

explanation.surface: A pay packet that has to cover rent and pressure leaves someone short.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deficient lacks a needed part, so it is incomplete.

clue.text: Smart maths done ignoring all tips for race

indicators.note: ignoring all tips means each of the three words loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A clever student finishes the maths homework without bothering with the hints, then goes off to run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' looks like advice; here it means the ends of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a long-distance running race of about 26 miles.

clue.text: Holds up baskets

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means hinders or holds up
large lidded baskets, often for picnics

explanation.surface: Something delays the delivery of picnic baskets.
explanation.definitionFit: Hampers is both a verb for obstructing progress and the plural of a lidded wicker basket.

clue.text: Mobile north side of city becomes troublesome

indicators.note: mobile means moving about, so the letters of north are rearranged
side of picks one edge letter of city, here its last

explanation.surface: The north side of a city turns into a problem area.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny problem is a prickly, difficult one, so thorny means troublesome.

clue.text: Rat sick with love for second one

indicators.note: for second says a letter replaces the second of the matching letters in the word for sick

parts.note: infirm means ill or sick
I is the Roman numeral for one
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A sick rat swaps its love for another one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat' is a verb here: to betray by telling.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat on someone is to inform on them to the authorities.

clue.text: Small organisms, hundred on piece of wood

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means one piece comes after the other

parts.note: a plank is a long flat piece of timber
a ton is informal for a hundred

explanation.surface: A hundred tiny creatures are found on a plank of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are the tiny plants and animals drifting in seas and lakes.

clue.text: About to be disciplined with respect to athletics event

parts.note: for can mean concerning or with respect to, as in so much for that
the high jump is a track-and-field event

explanation.surface: A coach discussing an athlete's high jump also hints someone is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the high jump' is a British idiom meaning about to be punished.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from the gallows: someone due to be hanged was for the high jump, so in for punishment.

clue.text: Eclipse on display, when crossing middle of meadow

parts.note: over can mean on top of, so on gives over

indicators.note: crossing here means the display word straddles the middle letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a show is a display

indicators.note: middle of picks the two central letters of meadow

explanation.surface: An eclipse on show as its shadow sweeps across a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshadow is to outshine or put in the shade, as one person eclipses another.

clue.text: Canadian neighbour in Toronto had illness coming back

indicators.note: coming back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the run of words Toronto had illness

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone in Toronto was ill on their return home.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' unassigned; it is the signal that the letters are tucked inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a US state bordering the Canadian province of British Columbia.

clue.text: Pass water day back, seeing bass

indicators.note: back says the pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: to pee is to pass water, urinate

explanation.surface: A fisherman relieves himself the day after catching a bass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bass' is the adjective for a low-pitched voice, not the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass voice is a deep one, the lowest male singing range.

clue.text: Stopping promotion

definitions.meaning: ... a hole is stopping it up
... a product is giving it publicity

explanation.definitionFit: Plugging means both blocking up a gap and giving something a publicity push.

clue.text: Second cold chip

parts.note: hard can mean harsh and cold, as in a hard winter

explanation.surface: Another chip that has gone cold, a sad plate of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A shard is a broken fragment of glass or pottery, a chip broken off.

clue.text: Dean half-cut on organ offers transfer

indicators.note: half-cut says only half of the word dean is kept, its first two letters

parts.note: the liver is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: A drunken dean at the organ offers to hand over a parish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk; here it trims DEAN to its first half.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver goods is to hand them over, a transfer from one person to another.

clue.text: Still recalled interview with odd characters getting rejected

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the remaining letters are read backwards
the letters of interview in odd-numbered places are thrown out, keeping only those in between

explanation.surface: A rejected candidate was still called back for interview despite some odd answers.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the odd letters of INTERVIEW leaves NEVE, which 'recalled' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Still and even both intensify a comparison, as in still better or even better.

clue.text: Air Force officer from Queens flying with old radar

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters whirling about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An officer from Queens flies an aircraft fitted with old radar.
explanation.definitionFit: A squadron leader is an RAF rank, equivalent to a major in the army.

clue.text: Pollution choking city guide

indicators.note: choking says the dirt wraps around the city, holding it inside

parts.note: dirt is filth or pollution
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Smog chokes a city, and someone must guide people through it.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is London's financial district, the City.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct someone is to guide or steer them on their way.

clue.text: Get at article within container

indicators.note: within says the article is placed inside the container word

parts.note: a tin is a metal container
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Reach into a container and grab the item inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain something is to get it by effort, a synonym of achieve.

clue.text: Pestered about branded clothes

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here, so the branded word dresses or wraps around the other

parts.note: badged means marked with a badge or brand
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone was nagged about wearing designer-label clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester them persistently, like a badger being baited.

clue.text: Several wanting Germany instead of Southern Hemisphere

indicators.note: instead of says one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: some means several, an unspecified number
D is the international vehicle code for Germany, Deutschland

explanation.surface: Several are missing Germany in a quiz on the Southern Hemisphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Southern Hemisphere' reads as one phrase; split it: 'Southern' is S and 'Hemisphere' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dome is a rounded roof shaped like half a sphere.

clue.text: Interior organs taxidermist originally stored in bottles

indicators.note: stored in says one letter is kept inside the bottles word

parts.note: vials are small bottles

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of taxidermist

explanation.surface: A taxidermist keeps an animal's innards preserved in jars.
explanation.definitionFit: The vitals are the vital organs inside the body, such as heart and lungs.

clue.text: Metal cable

explanation.definitionFit: Lead names both the soft heavy metal and an electrical cable connecting a device.

clue.text: Cold is able to disappear after knocking back alcohol

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: knocking back means turning back, so the pieces read in reverse

parts.note: can means is able to
to go can mean to disappear, as in the pain will go

explanation.surface: A chill can be shaken off after downing a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' suggests drinking; here it reverses CAN GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, a type of strong alcoholic spirit.

clue.text: Spoil American for nothing with an addition to cake

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
zip is American slang for nothing, zero

explanation.surface: Someone ruins an American bake by adding nothing extra.
explanation.definitionFit: Marzipan is an almond paste layered on fruit cakes beneath the icing, a topping added to cake.
